title: Incorrect permission assignment (CWE-732) in the standalone installer for EA Javelin Anticheat (versions 1.0.14329371, 1.0.14547437, 1.0.14789537,… (CVE-2026-96542)
description: An incorrect permission assignment vulnerability (CWE-732) exists in the standalone installer for EA Javelin Anticheat on Windows versions 1.0.14329371, 1.0.14547437, 1.0.14789537, and 1.0.14940698. This flaw allows a local non-administrative user to elevate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM by modifying the service configuration and executable path of the EAAntiCheatService. The vulnerability requires manual execution of the standalone installer and does not affect standard game installations via the EA App or Steam. The issue is fixed in version 1.0.14940699 and later, with service permissions self-healing when launching an integrated EA game title.
aiSummary: CVE-2026-96542 describes a privilege escalation vulnerability due to incorrect permission assignment (CWE-732) in the standalone installer for EA Javelin Anticheat on Windows. A local non-administrative user can exploit this by modifying the EAAntiCheatService service configuration and executable path, gaining SYSTEM-level privileges. This requires manual, non-standard execution of the standalone installer and does not impact installations through EA App or Steam. The vulnerability is resolved in version 1.0.14940699 and later, where service permissions automatically self-heal upon launching an integrated EA game.
aiImpact: A local attacker with limited privileges can escalate to SYSTEM privileges by exploiting the incorrect permission assignment in the standalone installer. This could lead to high confidentiality impact due to elevated access, with limited integrity impact and no availability impact as per the CVSS vector. The vulnerability is limited to manual installer execution and does not affect standard game installations.
